main_text.l: singulos, voluntas. Cum Dauide igitur canamus: Nō timebo à multis myriadibus populi, qui undique sese opponunt mihi. Exurge Iehouah, serua me Deus meus: Sanè percute omnes inimicos meos in maxilla, dentes eorum contere. Pfalm. 3. 6, 7.

Ne igitur opinemur, tum maximè periclitari Ecclesiam, cum tyranni θυμαχοι[?] omni genere armorum eam oppugnant: ut factum est temporibus Antiochi Epiphanis, Neronis, Diocletiani: & ut hac nostra ætate factu uidimus in uicinis quibusdam regnis. Sed tum demum in periculo esse, & graviter tentari & periclitari statuamus, cum longæ pacis incommoda sentit, & cum ij qui Ecclesiæ primarij Antistites uideri uolunt, prodigiosa dogmata in Ecclesiam inuehunt, dijudicandæ prophetiæ iuris sedentibus in Ecclesia eripiunt, & in conseruos sequiunt anathe-matismis, proscriptionibus, & alijs præ-sidijs deploratæ caussæ. Sedenim uiuit & regnat omnipotens ille & verax Ec-clesiæ suo sanguine redemptæ Defensor CHRISTVS IESVS, qui non nimium indulgebit licentiæ, quam φιλοπρωτευοντις[?]

page.notes: Long s is normalised to plain s throughout. "factum" and "factu" are printed with the st/ct ligature, read here as ct. The Greek word after "tyranni" is smudged and read with doubt. The last Greek word is at the line end and is only partly legible. The line-end Greek is continued on the next page, where "Dio-" is the catchword. The bare reference "Pfalm.3.6,7." is kept in the text as printed.
